figures.ask_en: What test is this, and what exactly does each plate show?
figures.ask_zh: 這是什麼測試？兩個培養皿各顯示什麼？
figures.a_en: The cell retention and sterility assessment of the shell-side permeate. Plate (a) is lumen-side medium sampled after running 24 hours in the bioreactor, and it shows colonies. Plate (b) is shell-side medium from the same run, and no colony grew. It is the evidence behind the one containment claim this project makes, and it is one plating from one run.
figures.a_zh: 這是殼側透過液的細胞截留與無菌性評估。(a) 是在反應器中運轉 24 小時後取的管腔側培養基，有長出菌落。(b) 是同一次實驗的殼側培養基，沒有任何菌落長出來。這是整個專題唯一一個圍堵宣稱背後的證據，而它是一次實驗的一次塗盤。
figures.q_en: What does plate (b) in this figure represent?
figures.q_zh: 這張圖裡的 (b) 培養皿代表什麼？
opt_en: Shell-side medium after 24 hours in the bioreactor, with no colonies grown
An uninoculated LB plate used as a sterility control
Lumen-side medium diluted one thousand fold
The same plate before incubation
opt_zh: 在反應器中跑了 24 小時後的殼側培養基，沒有長出菌落
未接種的 LB 培養皿，作為無菌對照
稀釋一千倍的管腔側培養基
同一個培養皿在培養之前的樣子
figures.trap_en: Calling this a validated containment system. It is a single, honest result and we say so on the page.
figures.trap_zh: 把它說成已驗證的圍堵系統。它是單一一次、我們誠實標示出來的結果，頁面上就是這樣寫的。

figures.ask_en: What is the white cartridge, and what role does it play in biosafety?
figures.ask_zh: 那個白色濾芯是什麼？它在生物安全上扮演什麼角色？
figures.a_en: The hollow fiber membrane cartridge mounted upright in the bioreactor case, with the tubing that carries the culture through it and the medium bottle beside it. Its 0.2 micrometre pore wall is the physical containment: the cells are wider than any pore so they stay in the lumen, while the secreted protectant crosses to the shell. After Dr. Brophy's advice this became the project's primary biosafety mechanism, in place of a kill switch.
figures.a_zh: 這是中空纖維膜濾芯，直立安裝在反應器機箱裡，旁邊是把菌液送過它的管路與培養基瓶。它 0.2 微米的孔壁就是實體圍堵：細胞比任何孔都大，所以留在管腔裡，而分泌出來的保護劑可以穿到殼側。在 Brophy 博士建議之後，這變成整個專題主要的生物安全機制，取代了自殺開關。
kw_en: primary containment, not a kill switch
kw_zh: 主要圍堵，不是自殺開關
figures.q_en: Why does this cartridge appear on the Safety page at all?
figures.q_zh: 這個濾芯為什麼會出現在安全頁上？
opt_en: Because it is the project's primary physical containment, keeping cells in while the protectant crosses
Because it is the component most likely to fail and cause a spill
Because it must be autoclaved before every run
Because it is classed as a controlled item under Taiwanese law
opt_zh: 因為它是專題主要的實體圍堵，把細胞留住、讓保護劑通過
因為它是最可能故障並造成洩漏的元件
因為每次實驗前都必須高壓滅菌
因為它在台灣法規下屬於列管品項
figures.trap_en: Describing containment only as lab practice. Here the containment is a component, which is why it belongs in the hardware answer too.
figures.trap_zh: 只把圍堵講成實驗室作業規範。在這裡圍堵是一個零件，所以它也屬於硬體那一題的答案。

figures.ask_en: What is on this door, and what biosafety level does it name?
figures.ask_zh: 這扇門上貼的是什麼？它標的是哪一個生物安全等級？
figures.a_en: Three posters on the lab door: the GEMS Academy laboratory rules, a Laboratory Area sign and a chart of the GHS hazard pictograms. The Laboratory Area sign lists biological hazard, toxic and poison materials, and P1 laboratory, together with the required personal protective equipment: lab coat, gloves, long trousers and closed-toe shoes. The emergency contact table is blurred in the published photograph.
figures.a_zh: 實驗室門上貼了三張：GEMS Academy 的實驗室規則、一張 Laboratory Area 標示，以及 GHS 危害圖示表。Laboratory Area 標示上列出生物危害、毒性物質，以及 P1 實驗室，還有必備的個人防護裝備：實驗衣、手套、長褲與包鞋。公開照片上的緊急聯絡人表格做了模糊處理。
kw_en: PPE: coat, gloves, trousers, closed shoes
kw_zh: 防護：實驗衣、手套、長褲、包鞋
figures.q_en: What laboratory classification does the sign in this photograph name?
figures.q_zh: 這張照片裡的標示上寫的是哪一個實驗室分級？
opt_en: P1 laboratory
P3 laboratory
A cleanroom of ISO class 7
A GMP manufacturing area
opt_zh: P1 實驗室
P3 實驗室
ISO 7 級無塵室
GMP 製造區
figures.trap_en: Not knowing your own containment level. P1 is the right answer and it should come without hesitation.
figures.trap_zh: 不知道自己實驗室的圍堵等級。答案是 P1，應該要不假思索講得出來。

figures.ask_en: What two things are overlaid on this map, and why put them together?
figures.ask_zh: 這張地圖疊了哪兩種資料？為什麼要疊在一起？
figures.a_en: Counties shaded by the average age of farmers in 2016, from 55 years in pale yellow to 61 and over in dark blue, with dark red circles at the weather stations sized by temperature change from 1991 to 2020. The overlay asks whether the counties facing the most heat stress are also the ones with the oldest farmers, which is a question about who will have to adapt and how much capacity they have to do it.
figures.a_zh: 縣市底色是 2016 年農民平均年齡，淡黃色 55 歲到深藍色 61 歲以上；上面疊的是各氣象站的深紅色圓圈，大小代表 1991 到 2020 年的溫度變化。這個疊圖問的是：承受最多熱逆境的縣市，是不是也是農民最高齡的縣市——這是在問「誰得去適應」以及「他們有多少餘力去適應」。
figures.q_en: What do the dark red circles on this map represent?
figures.q_zh: 這張地圖上的深紅色圓圈代表什麼？
opt_en: Temperature change at each weather station from 1991 to 2020, sized by magnitude
Rice production volume by county in 2024
The locations of farms the team actually visited
The number of farmers over 65 in each county
opt_zh: 各氣象站 1991 到 2020 年的溫度變化，圓圈大小代表幅度
2024 年各縣市的稻米產量
團隊實際拜訪過的農場位置
各縣市 65 歲以上農民的人數
figures.trap_en: Reading an overlay as a correlation that has been tested. The map poses the question; it does not report a statistic.
figures.trap_zh: 把疊圖當成已經檢定過的相關性。這張圖提出的是問題，不是統計結果。

figures.ask_en: What is mapped here, and why is this particular window of the year chosen?
figures.ask_zh: 這張圖畫的是什麼？為什麼挑這一段時間？
figures.a_en: The change in November to December minimum temperature between 1961-1990 and 2015-2024, by county, from 0 to 1.0 degrees in pale yellow up to 1.9 to 2.05 degrees in dark red. Miaoli, Taichung, Nantou, Chiayi, Tainan and Kaohsiung are the darkest. That window is tomato flowering: warm nights during flowering cut fruit set, so a night-warming map over those two months is the one that matters for tomato yield.
figures.a_zh: 這張畫的是各縣市 11 到 12 月最低溫，從 1961–1990 年到 2015–2024 年的變化，淡黃是 0 到 1.0 度，深紅是 1.9 到 2.05 度。苗栗、台中、南投、嘉義、台南、高雄最深。這一段時間正是番茄的開花期：開花期夜溫偏高會降低著果率，所以針對這兩個月做的夜間暖化圖，才是對番茄產量真正有意義的那一張。
figures.q_en: Why does this map cover November and December specifically?
figures.q_zh: 這張地圖為什麼特別只看 11 月與 12 月？
opt_en: Because that is the tomato flowering window, when warm nights cut fruit set
Because those are the only months with complete station records
Because the rice second crop is harvested then
Because the team's field visits happened in those months
opt_zh: 因為那是番茄的開花期，夜溫偏高會降低著果率
因為只有那兩個月的測站紀錄是完整的
因為二期稻作在那時候收割
因為團隊的田間拜訪發生在那兩個月
figures.trap_en: Showing a warming map with no crop window attached. The biology is what turns a climate map into an agricultural claim.
figures.trap_zh: 拿一張暖化圖出來卻沒有扣住作物的時期。有生物學上的理由，氣候圖才變成農業上的主張。

figures.ask_en: What experiment is this flow chart, and what is the result?
figures.ask_zh: 這張流程圖是什麼實驗？結果是什麼？
figures.a_en: A validation of our structured geospatial prompt against a plain-language one. The same 15,138-row dataset and the same question go to both. The structured prompt checks coordinate range and coordinate reference system, flags a precision problem (only 3,739 unique points), applies the filter and returns 2,502 rows. The plain-language prompt checks only for missing values, applies no filter and hands back all 15,138 rows. The structured prompt is the one that catches the data problem.
figures.a_zh: 這是把我們的結構化地理空間提示詞，拿來跟自然語言提示詞做驗證比較。同一份 15,138 列的資料、同一個問題，分別送給兩者。結構化提示詞會檢查座標範圍與座標參考系統，標出精度問題（只有 3,739 個不重複的點），套用篩選條件後回傳 2,502 列。自然語言提示詞只檢查缺失值，不做任何篩選，把 15,138 列原封不動丟回來。能抓到資料問題的是結構化提示詞。
kw_zh: 同樣 15,138 列、兩種提示詞
結構化版標出 3,739 個不重複點
figures.q_en: What did the structured prompt catch that the plain-language prompt missed?
figures.q_zh: 結構化提示詞抓到了什麼是自然語言提示詞漏掉的？
opt_en: A coordinate precision problem: only 3,739 unique points among 15,138 rows
That the dataset was in the wrong units of temperature
That the county names were spelled inconsistently
That the file had been truncated during download
opt_zh: 座標精度問題：15,138 列裡只有 3,739 個不重複的點
資料集的溫度單位用錯了
縣市名稱拼寫不一致
檔案在下載過程中被截斷
figures.trap_en: Presenting prompt engineering as a style preference. Here it is tested: same data, same question, two different answers, and only one of them notices the problem.
figures.trap_zh: 把提示詞工程講成個人風格偏好。這裡是真的做了測試：同樣的資料、同樣的問題、兩個不同的答案，而只有一個注意到問題。

figures.ask_en: What is happening here, and why does it matter for the education claim?
figures.ask_zh: 這裡在做什麼？它對教育的主張為什麼重要？
figures.a_en: Elementary students at laptops answering a Kahoot quiz at the start of a lesson: the pre-survey. It matters because it is the baseline. Everything we claim about knowledge growth in the elementary programme rests on having asked the same questions before the lesson as after it, across four different visits.
figures.a_zh: 國小學生在課程一開始用筆電作答 Kahoot 測驗：這是前測。它之所以重要，是因為它就是基線。我們對國小課程「知識有成長」的所有主張，都建立在「同樣的題目在課前問過、課後再問一次」這件事上，而且做了四次不同的拜訪。
figures.q_en: Why is this pre-survey the important part of the education programme?
figures.q_zh: 為什麼這份前測是整個教育課程中重要的部分？
opt_en: It is the baseline that lets the team claim knowledge growth rather than just a good score
It decides which students are allowed to do the experiment
It is how the team recruited volunteers for the forum
It replaces the written lab report at the end of the lesson
opt_zh: 它是基線，讓團隊可以宣稱「知識有成長」，而不只是「分數不錯」
它決定哪些學生可以做實驗
這是團隊替論壇招募志工的方式
它取代了課程結束時的書面實驗報告
figures.trap_en: Reporting a post-lesson score with nothing to compare it to. The forum KAP survey has exactly that weakness; the school programme does not.
figures.trap_zh: 報一個課後分數卻沒有東西可以對照。論壇的 KAP 問卷就是這個弱點，而國小課程沒有。

figures.ask_en: What experiment is being demonstrated, and what does it teach?
figures.ask_zh: 這裡示範的是什麼實驗？它在教什麼？
figures.a_en: A team member demonstrating the spinach leaf-disk experiment to elementary students around a table. Leaf disks sink in bicarbonate solution and float again as photosynthesis fills them with oxygen, so the class watches the rate of photosynthesis directly, with no instrument. It is the hands-on half of the lesson that the pre and post survey then measures.
figures.a_zh: 隊員在桌邊向國小學生示範菠菜葉圓盤實驗。葉圓盤放進碳酸氫鈉溶液中會沉下去，隨著光合作用產生氧氣又浮起來，所以全班不需要任何儀器就能直接看到光合作用的速率。這是課程中動手的那一半，而前後測量的就是這一段的效果。
figures.q_en: What makes the leaf-disk experiment suitable for an elementary classroom?
figures.q_zh: 葉圓盤實驗為什麼適合國小教室？
opt_en: The disks float as photosynthesis produces oxygen, so the rate is visible with no instrument
It uses the same photometer the team built for the bioreactor
It demonstrates DNA base pairing with coloured cards
It requires a biosafety cabinet, which the school already has
opt_zh: 光合作用產生氧氣後圓盤會浮起來，不用任何儀器就看得到速率
它用的是團隊替反應器做的那台光度計
它用彩色卡片示範 DNA 鹼基配對
它需要生物安全櫃，而學校剛好有
figures.trap_en: Confusing the leaf-disk experiment with the ATCG card game. Both are in the lesson; only one of them is about photosynthesis.
figures.trap_zh: 把葉圓盤實驗跟 ATCG 卡牌遊戲搞混。兩個都在課程裡，但只有一個是在講光合作用。

figures.ask_en: What are the students playing, and which concept does it carry?
figures.ask_zh: 學生在玩什麼？它承載的是哪一個概念？
figures.a_en: The ATCG base-pairing card game: elementary students around a table holding cards, matching bases while a team member watches. It carries DNA complementarity, the idea that A pairs with T and C with G, in a form a ten-year-old can play. The pre and post survey shows the related question, DNA codons, moving from 25 percent correct to 89 percent.
figures.a_zh: 這是 ATCG 鹼基配對卡牌遊戲：國小學生圍著桌子拿著卡片配對，隊員在旁邊看著。它承載的是 DNA 互補配對的概念——A 配 T、C 配 G——而且做成十歲小孩玩得動的形式。前後測顯示相關的那一題（DNA 密碼子）從 25% 答對提升到 89%。
figures.q_en: What concept does the ATCG card game teach?
figures.q_zh: ATCG 卡牌遊戲教的是哪一個概念？
opt_en: DNA base pairing: A with T and C with G
The difference between biotic and abiotic stress
The inputs and outputs of photosynthesis
How a bioreactor keeps bacteria contained
opt_zh: DNA 鹼基配對：A 配 T、C 配 G
生物性逆境與非生物性逆境的差別
光合作用的輸入與輸出
生物反應器怎麼把細菌關住
figures.trap_en: Describing outreach as activities. Each activity here maps to a survey question, and that mapping is the evidence.
figures.trap_zh: 把推廣講成「我們辦了哪些活動」。這裡每個活動都對應到一道問卷題目，那個對應才是證據。

figures.ask_en: What is this booth, and what is the blue board in the middle?
figures.ask_zh: 這個攤位是什麼？中間那塊藍板是什麼？
figures.a_en: Our data physicalization booth at the public forum, in an outdoor market. The blue board headed 作物的感官警報 is the sound exhibit, with the headphones on the table in front of it for listeners. The bioreactor prototype sits beside it, and the styrofoam stress map of Taiwan is the other exhibit. The idea is that a visitor hears and touches the stress data rather than reading a chart of it.
figures.a_zh: 這是我們在戶外市集公眾論壇上的資料實體化攤位。中間那塊標題為「作物的感官警報」的藍板是聲音展件，前面桌上擺著給聽眾用的耳機。旁邊放著反應器原型，另一個展件是保麗龍做的台灣逆境地圖。概念是：讓參觀者用聽的、用摸的去接觸逆境資料，而不是去看一張圖表。
kw_en: blue board is the sound exhibit
kw_zh: 用聽的用摸的，不是用讀的
figures.q_en: What is the blue board in the middle of this booth?
figures.q_zh: 這個攤位中間那塊藍板是什麼？
opt_en: The sound exhibit, with headphones on the table in front of it
The project poster explaining the genetic circuit
The styrofoam stress map of Taiwan
The KAP survey sign-up sheet
opt_zh: 聲音展件，前面桌上放著耳機
解釋基因線路的專題海報
保麗龍做的台灣逆境地圖
KAP 問卷的報名表
figures.trap_en: Describing the booth as a poster stand. The point of data physicalization is the sense the data arrives through.
figures.trap_zh: 把攤位講成海報展示區。資料實體化的重點是：資料是透過哪一種感官傳進來的。

figures.ask_en: What is on this screen, and what is actually being plotted?
figures.ask_zh: 這個畫面上是什麼？實際畫出來的是什麼？
figures.a_en: The listening site, with the header reading Tobacco, Drought and a counter showing 0 of 27 clicks played. Below it is a scatter of pitch in kilohertz against seconds into the recording, with a shaded band marked 40 to 80 kilohertz as the typical range, and a note that bigger dots mean louder clicks. These are the ultrasonic clicks a drought-stressed plant emits, drawn as data and played as sound.
figures.a_zh: 這是聆聽網站的畫面，標題寫著「Tobacco, Drought」，計數器顯示 27 個喀噠聲中播放了 0 個。下面是一張散佈圖，縱軸是音高（千赫），橫軸是錄音的秒數，陰影帶標出 40 到 80 千赫的典型範圍，旁邊註明點越大代表聲音越大。這些是乾旱逆境下植物發出的超音波喀噠聲，既畫成資料也播成聲音。
figures.q_en: What does each dot on this scatter represent?
figures.q_zh: 這張散佈圖上的每一個點代表什麼？
opt_en: One ultrasonic click from a stressed plant, placed by pitch and time, sized by loudness
One visitor's response to the booth survey
One weather station reading of night temperature
One seedling's chlorophyll measurement
opt_zh: 逆境下植物發出的一個超音波喀噠聲，依音高與時間定位，大小代表音量
一位參觀者對攤位問卷的回答
一個氣象站的夜溫讀值
一株幼苗的葉綠素量測值
figures.trap_en: Presenting the plant sounds as our own measurement. These are published recordings we made listenable, not data we collected.
figures.trap_zh: 把植物的聲音說成我們自己量的。那是已發表的錄音，我們把它做成可以聽的形式，不是我們蒐集的資料。

figures.ask_en: What is this chart, and which bar is the green one?
figures.ask_zh: 這是什麼圖？綠色那條是哪一個？
figures.a_en: The knowledge question from the booth survey: which region has the highest plant stress. Yilan County, marked as the correct answer, is the green bar at 51.6 percent, 32 of 62 respondents. Kaohsiung is 19.4 percent, Taichung 17.7 and Tainan 11.3, all grey. It is the data physicalization page's own version of the KAP knowledge result.
figures.a_zh: 這是攤位問卷的知識題：哪一個地區的植物逆境最嚴重。被標為正確答案的宜蘭縣是綠色長條，51.6%，62 人中有 32 人。高雄 19.4%、台中 17.7%、台南 11.3%，都是灰色。這是資料實體化頁上自己呈現的 KAP 知識結果版本。
kw_en: which region has the highest stress
figures.q_en: What was the question behind this chart?
figures.q_zh: 這張圖背後問的是什麼問題？
opt_en: Which region of Taiwan has the highest plant stress
Which exhibit at the booth visitors enjoyed most
Whether visitors would share what they learned with family
Which crop visitors thought was most at risk
opt_zh: 台灣哪一個地區的植物逆境最嚴重
參觀者最喜歡攤位上的哪一個展件
參觀者會不會把學到的事情分享給家人
參觀者認為哪一種作物風險最高
figures.trap_en: Mixing the knowledge chart up with the attitude and practice charts. Knowledge is the one with a right answer.
figures.trap_zh: 把知識題的圖跟態度題、行為題的圖搞混。知識題才是有正確答案的那一種。

figures.ask_en: What does this chart measure, and which question moved most?
figures.ask_zh: 這張圖量的是什麼？哪一題進步最多？
figures.a_en: Knowledge growth across seven questions, pre-survey against post-survey, from four elementary school visits. Correct responses rose from 18 to 82 percent on the purpose of photosynthesis, 81 to 93 on its inputs, 31 to 88 on its outputs, 16 to 91 on biotic versus abiotic stress, 65 to 86 on identifying a biotic stressor, 25 to 89 on DNA codons, and 74 to 92 on climate change impact. Biotic versus abiotic stress moved most, from 16 to 91.
figures.a_zh: 這張量的是七個題目的知識成長，前測對後測，來自四次國小拜訪。答對率的變化：光合作用的目的從 18% 到 82%，光合作用的輸入從 81% 到 93%，輸出從 31% 到 88%，生物性與非生物性逆境的分辨從 16% 到 91%，辨識生物性逆境源從 65% 到 86%，DNA 密碼子從 25% 到 89%，氣候變遷影響從 74% 到 92%。進步最多的是生物性與非生物性逆境的分辨，從 16% 到 91%。
kw_en: pre and post survey, seven questions
kw_zh: 生物／非生物逆境 16% 到 91%
figures.q_en: Which question showed the largest gain between pre- and post-survey?
figures.q_zh: 哪一題在前後測之間的進步幅度最大？
opt_en: Biotic versus abiotic stress, from 16 to 91 percent correct
The inputs of photosynthesis, from 81 to 93 percent
Climate change impact, from 74 to 92 percent
Identifying a biotic stressor, from 65 to 86 percent
opt_zh: 生物性與非生物性逆境的分辨，從 16% 到 91%
光合作用的輸入，從 81% 到 93%
氣候變遷的影響，從 74% 到 92%
辨識生物性逆境源，從 65% 到 86%
figures.trap_en: Quoting the highest post-survey number instead of the biggest gain. A question that started at 81 percent had little room to move.
figures.trap_zh: 引用後測最高分而不是進步最多的那一題。本來就 81% 的題目，本來就沒有多少進步空間。

figures.ask_en: What level is this class, and which SDG does this work sit under?
figures.ask_zh: 這堂課是哪個學制？這項工作歸在哪一個 SDG 下？
figures.a_en: A team member teaching a high school class in front of a slide reading Abiotic vs Biotic Stress. On the Sustainability page this sits under SDG 4, quality education: the problem we name there is that many people carry misconceptions about synthetic biology because the only accessible material is scientific papers that are hard to read. Teaching across three school levels is our answer to that.
figures.a_zh: 隊員在一張標題為「Abiotic vs Biotic Stress」的投影片前，對高中班級授課。在永續頁上，這項工作歸在 SDG 4（優質教育）之下：我們在那裡指出的問題是，很多人對合成生物學抱持誤解，因為唯一拿得到的材料是難讀的科學論文。跨三個學制去上課，就是我們對這件事的回應。
figures.q_en: Which SDG does the Sustainability page file this teaching work under?
figures.q_zh: 永續頁把這項教學工作歸在哪一個 SDG 下？
opt_en: SDG 4, quality education
SDG 2, zero hunger
SDG 15, life on land
SDG 12, responsible consumption
opt_zh: SDG 4，優質教育
SDG 2，消除飢餓
SDG 15，陸域生態
SDG 12，負責任的消費
figures.trap_en: Listing SDGs without saying which piece of work sits under each. The page pairs every goal with a specific problem and a specific action.
figures.trap_zh: 只列 SDG 卻不講哪一項工作歸在哪一個底下。頁面上每一個目標都配著一個具體問題與一個具體行動。

figures.ask_en: What are the rows and columns here, and what does the last row show?
figures.ask_zh: 這張圖的行與列是什麼？最後一排顯示什麼？
figures.a_en: Hydroponic boxes photographed from above: columns are box 1 control, box 2 pre-treatment, box 3 co-treatment and box 4 post-treatment; rows are 25 July, 28 July and 4 August. By 4 August the co-treatment box carries the largest and greenest rosettes while the control and the post-treatment boxes have browned. On the Sustainability page it sits under SDG 2, zero hunger, as the evidence that the protectant can hold a crop through a stress.
figures.a_zh: 水耕盒由上方拍攝：四欄分別是第 1 盒對照、第 2 盒前處理、第 3 盒同時處理、第 4 盒後處理；三排是 7 月 25 日、7 月 28 日、8 月 4 日。到 8 月 4 日，同時處理那一盒的蓮座最大也最綠，對照組與後處理組則已經褐化。在永續頁上，它放在 SDG 2（消除飢餓）之下，作為「保護劑能幫作物撐過一次逆境」的證據。
kw_zh: 8 月 4 日同時處理最綠
figures.q_en: Which box is doing best by the last row of this figure?
figures.q_zh: 到這張圖最後一排為止，哪一盒狀況最好？
opt_en: Box 3, co-treatment
Box 1, the control
Box 2, pre-treatment
Box 4, post-treatment
opt_zh: 第 3 盒，同時處理
第 1 盒，對照組
第 2 盒，前處理
第 4 盒，後處理
figures.trap_en: Carrying this result across to the agar plates. The best timing differs between the hydroponic and agar systems and between protectants; name the system every time.
figures.trap_zh: 把這個結果直接套到洋菜盤上。最佳時機在水耕與洋菜系統之間、在不同保護劑之間都不一樣；每次都要講清楚是哪一個系統。

figures.ask_en: Walk this diagram from left to right in one breath.
figures.ask_zh: 一口氣把這張圖從左講到右。
figures.a_en: Plant stresses, an AIoT sensor that picks them up, a green light signal, B. subtilis carrying the CcaSR circuit, the hollow fiber membrane, protectant secretion, plant protected. Seven steps. It is the one diagram every member should be able to narrate without notes, because it names what senses, what decides, what makes and what contains.
figures.a_zh: 植物逆境、感測到逆境的 AIoT 感測器、綠光訊號、帶 CcaSR 線路的 B. subtilis、中空纖維膜、保護劑分泌、植物獲得保護。七個步驟。這是每一位隊員都應該不看稿就講得出來的那一張圖，因為它把「誰在感測、誰在決定、誰在製造、誰在圍堵」都講完了。
figures.q_en: What is the signal that carries the decision from the sensor to the bacteria?
figures.q_zh: 把決定從感測器傳到細菌的訊號是什麼？
opt_en: A green light signal, read by the CcaSR system in B. subtilis
A chemical inducer added to the medium
A change in the medium's pH
A temperature setpoint sent to the incubator
opt_zh: 綠光訊號，由 B. subtilis 的 CcaSR 系統接收
加進培養基的化學誘導物
培養基 pH 的改變
送給培養箱的溫度設定值
figures.trap_en: Skipping the sensor. The chain begins outside the reactor, with something in the field that notices a stress.
figures.trap_zh: 跳過感測器。這條鏈的起點在反應器之外，是田裡某個東西察覺到逆境。

figures.ask_en: What are the four modules, and which one would a judge most likely probe?
figures.ask_zh: 這四個模組是什麼？評審最可能追問哪一個？
figures.a_en: The genetic circuit inside B. subtilis, in four modules. Module 1, PCB synthesis, turns heme into phycocyanobilin with ho1::pcyA. Module 2, light sensing, is CcaS in the membrane, switched on by green light under stress and off by red light when there is none. Module 3, transcriptional output, is CcaR and its dimer. Module 4 is the output: translation and the folded protectant leaving the cell. Module 1 is the one to be ready on, because B. subtilis does not make PCB on its own and without it CcaS cannot see light at all.
figures.a_zh: 這是 B. subtilis 體內的基因線路，分成四個模組。模組 1 是 PCB 合成，用 ho1::pcyA 把血紅素變成藻藍膽素。模組 2 是光感測，CcaS 位在膜上，逆境時綠光把它打開，沒有逆境時紅光把它關掉。模組 3 是轉錄輸出，CcaR 與它的雙體。模組 4 是輸出：轉譯以及摺疊好的保護劑離開細胞。要準備好被問的是模組 1，因為 B. subtilis 自己做不出 PCB，沒有它 CcaS 根本看不到光。
figures.q_zh: 模組 1 的 ho1::pcyA 產生的是什麼？
opt_en: Phycocyanobilin, the chromophore CcaS needs in order to respond to light
The ACC deaminase protectant itself
The CcaR transcriptional regulator
The secretion signal peptide that exports the protectant
opt_zh: 藻藍膽素（PCB），CcaS 要能感光所需要的發色團
ACC 去胺酶保護劑本身
CcaR 轉錄調控因子
把保護劑送出細胞的分泌訊號胜肽
figures.trap_en: Describing the circuit as 'green light turns it on' and stopping there. Without module 1 there is nothing for the light to act on.
figures.trap_zh: 把線路講成「綠光一照就開」就停了。沒有模組 1，光根本沒有東西可以作用。

figures.ask_en: What two variables are on this map, and what is the claim it supports?
figures.ask_zh: 這張地圖上有哪兩個變數？它支持的主張是什麼？
figures.a_en: County nighttime temperature, 18:00 to midnight, averaged through 2024, in five bands from 20.51 to 27.26 degrees, blue to red. The white proportional circles are the rice yield trend at each station over 2005 to 2024, from minus 0.044 to plus 0.058 tonnes per hectare per year. The hottest counties are in the north and the south. It supports the opening claim that warm nights, not just hot days, are what is eroding rice yield in Taiwan.
figures.a_zh: 底色是各縣市 2024 年全年平均的夜間溫度（18:00 到午夜），分成 20.51 到 27.26 度五個級距，由藍到紅。白色的比例圓圈是各測站 2005 到 2024 年的稻作產量趨勢，從每年每公頃 −0.044 到 +0.058 公噸。最熱的縣市分布在北部與南部。它支持的是開場的那個主張：侵蝕台灣稻作產量的是暖夜，不只是熱天。
kw_en: warm nights, not just hot days
figures.q_en: What do the white proportional circles on this map show?
figures.q_zh: 這張地圖上的白色比例圓圈顯示什麼？
opt_en: The rice yield trend at each station over 2005 to 2024, in tonnes per hectare per year
The number of weather stations in each county
The area of farmland under rice in each county
The average age of farmers at each location
opt_zh: 各測站 2005 到 2024 年的稻作產量趨勢，單位是每年每公頃公噸
各縣市的氣象站數量
各縣市種稻的農地面積
各地點農民的平均年齡
figures.trap_en: Reading the map as proof of causation. It is the motivating picture; the causal work is the stress model on the Math Model page.
figures.trap_zh: 把這張地圖當成因果的證明。它是用來帶出動機的圖；真正做因果的是數學模型頁上的逆境模型。
